task: Revise only this synthetic Results passage to explain the layout-coverage comparison. This is authored development material, not real research or a blinded trial.
draft: We collect 600 demonstrations across 12 layouts. Our policy reaches 68% success. The baseline achieves 51%. These findings establish broad generalization.

evidence.E1: Both policies use 600 demonstrations, the same architecture, task mix and optimization budget. The varied-layout policy uses 12 training layouts; the narrow-layout baseline uses two.
evidence.E2: On the same six held-out layouts, with 40 trials per layout, the varied-layout policy has reported mean success of 68% and the narrow-layout baseline 51%.
evidence.E3: This comparison supports an advantage of broader training-layout coverage in this evaluation. Other tasks and types of distribution shift were not evaluated; no significance test is supplied.

S1.source: Original synthetic teaching observation, not a published paper
S1.choice: Introduce a matched control before interpreting a performance difference, so the reader can distinguish coverage from dataset size.
S1.applicability: The author's evidence must actually fix dataset size and relevant training conditions while varying coverage.
S1.non_transfer: Do not transfer another study's scores, infer statistical significance, or claim general robustness. The control can be placed in a preceding sentence rather than one prescribed sentence order.
